newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Technicals, rate fears drag SIMEX Euroyen lower.
newsitem.headline: Technicals, rate fears drag SIMEX Euroyen lower.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures slid lower on Wednesday on market concerns the Bank of Japan (BOJ) might end its policy of guiding the overnight call loan rate below the discount rate, signalling a possible change in its easy monetary policy stance.
Dealers said the market remained nervous after a BOJ official's comments on Tuesday about Japan's low long-term interest rates reflecting uncertainty about its economy.
"There's still talk that the BOJ might want to inflate rates in the money market so people are shifting from the short end to the long end of the curve," said a trader with a Japanese house.
He said speculation of a U.S. interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting on March 25 was fuelling the Japanese rate fears.
"If U.S. rates go up, Japan will have no choice but to raise rates. Otherwise their currency will get too weak," he said.
But a senior dealer at an Asian institution said the BOJ could not tighten rates even if the United States did. "Japan has its own set of problems," he said.
He said market participation was limited as many Japanese players were staying out ahead of their financial year end on March 31.
But he said December Euroyen was likely to remain supported around 99.00, and head higher after the BOJ's quarterly business sentiment survey on April 2.
"Traders feel JGBs are too high whereas this is a good level to go back into Euroyen," he said.
December Euroyen stood at 99.04 at 1120 GMT, one tick above an intra-day low, against its IMM close at 99.10 on volume of 32,605 lots.
A trader with a U.S. house said heavy stop-loss sales were triggered at 99.05 early in the day, but the contract was likely to head higher and consolidate around 99.10.
June JGBs ended at 126.09 against their previous 125.92 after hitting a low of 125.56.
Eurodollar futures finished little changed ahead of the release of the U.S. Consumer Price Index for February at 1330 GMT. September ended at 93.905 against its IMM close at 93.900.
